samples.summary: The new stale-`selectedImage` guard is only in `imageKeyHandler`; sibling paths that act on the same stored `{blockId, offset}` still use the throwing `doc.getBlock`, so a remote block delete crashes them
samples.evidence: The diff adds `doc.findBlock(...)` + `findImageAtOffset` at editor.ts:2262-2266 specifically because "the peer may have removed the block outright, and the throwing lookup would take this keydown listener down with it". The other consumers of the identical stale state were not converted: `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2447 `const block = doc.getBlock(blockId); ... block ? ... : null`), `getSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3677), `updateSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3690) and `selectImageAt` (editor.ts:3663). `Doc.getBlock` throws (`throw new Error('Block not found: ...')`, document.ts:187) rather than returning undefined, so each `if (!block) return` / `block ? ... : null` is dead code and the call throws out of a DOM event handler. Concretely reachable: select an image, start a resize drag, a peer deletes that block mid-drag, mouseup -> `doc.getBlock` throws, the `render()` at 2450 never runs and the exception escapes the mouseup listener.

samples.summary: The bare-modifier allowlist misses other modifier-ish keydowns (CapsLock, AltGraph, OS, ContextMenu, Dead/Process), which still fall into the catch-all and silently drop the image selection with no repaint
samples.evidence: `if (key === 'Meta' || key === 'Control' || key === 'Shift' || key === 'Alt') return false;` covers only four keys. A `CapsLock` (or AltGraph / ContextMenu / dead-key) keydown reaches the catch-all at 2365, which sets `selectedImage = null` and returns false without calling `render()`; TextEditor's switch has no case for those keys either, so nothing repaints. The resize handles stay painted over an image that is no longer selected, and the next Backspace/Delete acts on the caret rather than the image the user still sees selected — exactly the class of mismatch the diff's own comment says it is fixing for Meta/Control/Shift/Alt.

samples.summary: Copying an image inside a table cell silently leaves the previous clipboard contents, so the next paste replays unrelated content
samples.evidence: `if (layout.blockParentMap.get(blockId) === undefined)` skips promotion for cell blocks and the handler returns false with `selectedImage` still set. `handleCut`/`handleCopy` (text-editor.ts:1174, 1200) then bail on `!this.selection.hasSelection()` without `preventDefault`, so Cmd/Ctrl+C on a cell image writes nothing at all — the stale clipboard is pasted next, which is the same user-visible symptom as issue #870 that this change exists to fix, just narrowed to table cells. The code comment acknowledges the trade-off, but the behaviour is still wrong for the in-table case.

samples.summary: Platform detection via the deprecated `navigator.platform` makes the copy branch a no-op-plus-deselect where the value is empty/frozen
samples.evidence: `const isMac = /Mac|iPhone|iPad|iPod/.test(navigator.platform)` — when a browser reports an empty or frozen `navigator.platform` (Chrome has been reducing it) on macOS, `mod` becomes `e.ctrlKey`, so Cmd+C with an image selected does not match the branch, falls to the catch-all at 2365, clears `selectedImage`, and nothing is copied — the original #870 behaviour returns. TextEditor uses the same expression (text-editor.ts:858), so the failure is at least consistent, but the new clipboard path inherits it.

samples.summary: The tint test builds the image box without `pageY`, so its geometry does not match `DocCanvas` and the vertical half of the intersection test is never meaningfully exercised
samples.evidence: Production computes `y: pageY + pl.y + pl.line.height - drawH` (doc-canvas.ts:604) where `pageY = getPageYOffset(...) = Theme.pageGap + ...` (pagination.ts:199, non-zero even for page 0), while the test uses `y: pl.y + pl.line.height - drawH` and compares against `computeSelectionRects` output, which *does* include `pageY`. The tests still pass only because the constant `Theme.pageGap` shift is smaller than the image height, so every vertical comparison is trivially true; a y-axis regression in `imageIntersectsSelection` would not be caught by this suite.
searchedFor: pageY usage in doc-canvas.ts render loop

samples.summary: In read-only mode Cmd/Ctrl+X promotes and deselects the image while `handleCut` refuses to act, so the shortcut just silently loses the image selection
samples.evidence: The copy/cut branch does not consult `readOnly`; it sets `selectedImage = null` and installs a text range. `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1195-1198) preventDefaults and returns immediately when `this.readOnly`, so nothing is copied and nothing is cut — the only observable effect of Cmd/Ctrl+X on a view-only document is that the image's selection handles disappear.

finding.summary: The new stale-`selectedImage` guard is only in `imageKeyHandler`; sibling paths that act on the same stored `{blockId, offset}` still use the throwing `doc.getBlock`, so a remote block delete crashes them
finding.evidence: The diff adds `doc.findBlock(...)` + `findImageAtOffset` at editor.ts:2262-2266 specifically because "the peer may have removed the block outright, and the throwing lookup would take this keydown listener down with it". The other consumers of the identical stale state were not converted: `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2447 `const block = doc.getBlock(blockId); ... block ? ... : null`), `getSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3677), `updateSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3690) and `selectImageAt` (editor.ts:3663). `Doc.getBlock` throws (`throw new Error('Block not found: ...')`, document.ts:187) rather than returning undefined, so each `if (!block) return` / `block ? ... : null` is dead code and the call throws out of a DOM event handler. Concretely reachable: select an image, start a resize drag, a peer deletes that block mid-drag, mouseup -> `doc.getBlock` throws, the `render()` at 2450 never runs and the exception escapes the mouseup listener.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out. `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` (document.ts:187) and has a non-throwing twin `findBlock` (document.ts:193). The new stale-selection guard uses `findBlock` only inside `imageKeyHandler` (editor.ts:2262-2266), while `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2447-2448), `selectImageAt` (editor.ts:3663-3664), `getSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3677-3678) and `updateSelectedImage` (editor.ts:3690-3691) still call the throwing `getBlock` and then test a falsy result that can never occur — those `if (!block) return` / `block ? ... : null` arms are dead, and the call throws instead. The remote-delete scenario is real and unguarded for this state: `store.onRemoteChange` (docs-view.tsx:378-394) refreshes the doc and calls only `editor.validateCursorPosition()` (editor.ts:979-987, which fixes the cursor alone); no code path clears `selectedImage` or `imageResizeDrag` on a remote change (all assignments enumerated: editor.ts:2264/2274/2284/2301/2347/2365/2531/2541/3667/3672/3785, plus imageResizeDrag only at 2442 and 3786). So a resize drag begun at editor.ts:2505-2517 that outlives a peer's block deletion hits `doc.getBlock` at editor.ts:2447 on mouseup, the exception escapes the document-level mouseup listener and the `render()` calls at 2450/2454/2468 never run, leaving stale paint state. No refutation ground applies: code is present as described, reachable, and unhandled.
